source.title: Present but Rescaled: Chat-to-Agent Transfer of Additive Activation Steering

record.tranche_reason: The study measures chat-to-agent transfer of additive activation steering in a new deployment setting, reporting dose-response shifts for refusal-related behavior. It does not reproduce the original layer-and-position ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The reported install-site agent-over-chat ratios of 0.83–1.16 are attributed to prior work and are not this study's results, so they are not rows. The study's causal scaffold intervention was not launched; its reported attainability analysis is not a test of the refusal-direction claim.
record.test_reason: The study steers six chat models with the standard difference-of-means refusal direction, adding it (induce arm) or subtracting it (bypass arm), and sweeps dose in chat and in a ReAct agent scaffold. Its own results show the direction still raises or lowers refusal to matching plateaus in a new deployment setting, which bears on V1's addition claim. Its main estimand, the cross-context midpoint shift dEC50 and the gain ratio T, measures how much dose is needed. That is a related construct no version names. Chat-to-agent is not the language, model-variant or base-to-instruct transfer V6 names, so V6 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that a gain ratio read at one dose does not identify potency versus efficacy. The chat-extracted steering vector still works in the agent scaffold, with matching plateaus, but its half-maximal dose shifts, signed both ways and family-dependent. They recommend sweeping the dose-response curve in the deployment context. They also report that their pre-registered dEC50 forecaster was refuted out of sample, and that the causal scaffold experiment was not run.
record.recipe_differences: Uses additive activation steering and a chat-extracted direction in an agent context, but reports dose-response transfer rather than the original direction's all-layer/all-position ablation and addition tests. The text does not specify the study's direction extraction recipe in enough detail to establish an exact match.
record.method_sensitivity: Dose affects the gain ratio: the reported range contains 1 in every one of five scorable cells, and T moves with dose in four of five. The positive Llama shift loses CI exclusion under the registered α*-trim.

fits_no_version.finding: The dose needed to reach half-maximal refusal change differs between chat and agent scaffold, in both directions across models. dEC50 is +1.013 on Llama-3.1-8B induce and negative on OLMo-2-7B bypass, Qwen2.5-7B (both arms) and Gemma-3-12B. The single-dose gain ratio T spans 1 in every scorable cell.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction's dose-response location shifts when moving from chat to agent scaffolds, in a model-dependent direction, so chat-calibrated coefficients don't transfer.

record.problems: The study tests chat-to-agent transfer, not the original refusal-vector ablation claim. It reports only six distinct models and eight family-by-arm cells; the positive displacement rests on one model, and the authors report selection bias against positive shifts. The OLMo-2-7B induce cell is quarantined because the response inverts after coherence collapse. The combined binary metric remains length-correlated, the primary fit retains doses at or above the reported α* ceiling, and general capability is not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows omitted. Results cited from prior work, including direction-install ratios, were excluded.

untested.parts: Directional ablation (the bypass arm uses negative addition, not projection). Refusal of harmless requests. General capability after intervention; only an output-coherence flag is measured.
Harm judgment is not separated from refusal.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer. The direction is extracted per model.

missing.what: Fitted upper asymptotes (plateau refusal change) in chat vs agent per cell, agreeing within 0.012 (0.013 with Gemma). This is the direct evidence that addition or subtraction attains full refusal change in both contexts.
Chat swing gate (≥25pt refusal change in chat per family/arm). This is the size of the induced or bypassed refusal effect.
Coherence collapse with dose (coherent margin positive in 9 of 10 GREEN cell-context pairs; OLMo-2-7B induce h(30)=0.231, h(43)=0.010)

record.verdict_notes: The steering direction is the refusal difference-of-means (128 vs 128, last token) applied additively. The bypass arm subtracts it rather than ablating it. All extracted rows are dose-location or gain-estimator quantities, so they are relinked to none and recorded under fits_no_version. The V1 verdict rests on text-only results flagged in missing. Install-site ratios 0.83–1.16 are cited from the predecessor paper (Pinto 2026) and correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original difference-in-means direction's refusal mediation by projecting it out, nor does it separately test refusal of harmless requests or general capability after ablation/addition.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak attack that suppresses the direction and no training against its ablation are tested.
The study does not compare a single direction with an affine set, cone, or multiple-direction account.
It does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Tests transfer from chat to an agent scaffold only; it does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No refusal-training procedure, timing, or training-stage comparison is tested.

relationships.condition: Additive steering with the chat-extracted difference-of-means refusal direction, chat and ReAct agent contexts, 6 law-eligible cells over 5 models (Llama-3.1-8B, OLMo-2-7B, Qwen2.5-3B/7B, Gemma-3-12B)
relationships.reason: From the text, as no row records it. Every family passes a ≥25pt chat swing gate. Adding or subtracting the direction moves refusal to plateaus whose fitted asymptotes agree across contexts within 0.012–0.013. Coherence midpoints sit above behavioural midpoints in 9 of 10 margins.
relationships.display_finding: Every model family showed at least a 25-point chat refusal swing, fitted refusal asymptotes agreed across contexts within 0.012–0.013, and coherence midpoints exceeded behavioral midpoints in 9 of 10 comparisons.

relationships.condition: High doses, e.g. OLMo-2-7B induce at doses ≥30
relationships.reason: From the text: outputs collapse (coherent fraction 0.23 at dose 30, 0.01 at 43) and the agent response inverts. The refusal effect at high dose comes with degraded output.
relationships.display_finding: The coherent-output fraction fell to 0.23 at dose 30 and 0.01 at dose 43, accompanied by inversion of the agent response.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Chat-to-agent transfer in the tested model/arm cells
reader_labels.reason: Transfer is context-dependent in dose: reported dEC50 shifts and dose-varying gain ranges show that a chat-calibrated coefficient does not carry a fixed behavioral meaning into the agent scaffold (r1–r13).
